headlines.article_text: BlackRock profit jumps as resilient markets boost fees Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu In this article BLK Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT The BlackRock logo is pictured outside the company's headquarters in the Manhattan borough of New York City on May 25, 2021. Carlo Allegri | Reuters BlackRock posted a jump in third-quarter profit on Wednesday, as the world's largest asset manager raked in higher fees from managing client funds. The company's shares jumped nearly 4% in premarket trading. BlackRock's profit ⁠rose to $1.66 billion, or $10.57 per share, in the three months ended September 30, compared with $1.32 billion, or $8.43 per share, a year ​earlier. Assets under management — which determine ​a large chunk of ​the earnings — rose to $15.49 trillion, from $13.46 trillion a year earlier. The growth was driven by a combination of $134.5 billion of new flows into BlackRock's flagship iShares ETFs, and the rising valuations of its investments in a robust ⁠equity ‌market. "Market fundamentals are strong and well supported, with higher ⁠margins and earnings momentum catalyzed by new technology," CEO Larry Fink said in a statement. The benchmark S&P 500, which is trading close to its all-time highs fueled by a rally in AI-focused stocks, extended its steady climb in the quarter, while ‌investors continued to demonstrate their willingness to pour money into asset management firms such as BlackRock. Even as markets have remained sturdy, the combination of surging bond yields and ​the expectation that the Federal Reserve's recent interest rate hike marks the beginning of a tightening cycle has called into question whether the rally can be sustained. Higher yields over a sustained period can put pressure on markets as investors rotate capital into safe-haven assets, ⁠locking in better risk-adjusted returns. Net flows into BlackRock's debt products were $78.2 billion in the quarter, signaling strong investor appetite despite ‌the recent steep selloff in Treasuries. Private markets push BlackRock has accelerated its ‌push into private credit markets in recent years. The asset class typically generates higher fees than the firm's main source of profits, its suite of ETFs, which depends on high volumes of inflows to boost earnings. The company ⁠has spelled out plans to deliver more than $35 billion in revenue by the end of ⁠the decade, with over 30% of that coming from private markets and technology. The ⁠private credit industry has come under scrutiny by investors concerned about lenders' exposure to software companies seen as particularly vulnerable to disruption from AI, as well as ​the opacity of valuations in private markets. Those concerns ‌prompted a surge in redemption requests from investors in recent quarters. That backlog, however, seems to be easing, with most large managers of private credit funds reporting slowing redemption requests in the third quarter. BlackRock's HPS Corporate Lending Fund saw redemption requests fall to roughly 11.5% of shares in the latest quarter, down from 13.3% in the ​second quarter. While BlackRock doesn't break out its ‌revenue from private markets, net flows in this category were $15.31 billion in the quarter. headlines.article_text: ASML says it's getting order interest through 2030 on AI demand Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points ASML said some customers are "expressing an interest" in placing orders with the company in 2029 and 2030, providing investors with a view into longer-term demand. The Dutch chip giant said it is looking at ways to increase capacity for 2028 beyond the 30% increase it had previously forecast as demand remains strong. The company also raised the lower end of its sales forecast for 2026. In this article ASML TSM Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT ASML said Wednesday that some of its customers are expressing interest in placing orders for its critical semiconductor tools for 2029 and 2030 as the company reported third-quarter profit that beat expectations. The comments will likely comfort investors who have been looking to assess the longer-term demand outlook for ASML's lithography machines. "Our customers continue to increase their short- and medium-term equipment demand forecasts with us, driven primarily by their views on the size and duration of AI-related investments," CEO Christophe Fouquet said in a press release. "In light of their demand visibility, some customers are expressing an interest in placing orders with us for 2029 and even 2030." ASML is the only company in the world that produces extreme ultraviolet lithography machines, a key tool used by the likes of TSMC to make the world's most advanced semiconductors. Investors closely watch the Dutch company's earnings for signs of AI-related chip demand. watch now VIDEO 3:47 03:47 ASML races to expand capacity on strong AI-driven demand Squawk Box Europe Fouquet said current supply planned for 2027 and 2028 will not fully meet the demand of its customers. The company is "investigating ways" to increase capacity for 2028 beyond the 30% increase it had previously forecast. ASML has now updated its guidance three times this year, upping its full-year forecast for the second time in July, and on Wednesday it raised the lower end of its sales forecast for 2026. The company now expects net sales of between 44 billion euros and 45 billion euros ($49.3 billion to $50.4 billion). The previous lower end of the forecast was for 43 billion euros. ASML also said it expects fourth-quarter net sales of between 14.2 billion euros and 15.2 billion euros. The upper end of the range is ahead of LSEG consensus estimates of 14.2 billion euros. ASML's stock was around 2% higher in early trade in Europe. Shares of the company have rallied 56% this year. ASML shares year-to-date During the quarter, Samsung and TSMC, the world's two biggest chipmakers, committed to using ASML's High NA extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines. High NA EUV is ASML's next-generation tool, which analysts see as key to the Dutch firm's future growth. For the third quarter, here's how ASML did versus LSEG consensus estimates: Net sales: 11.66 billion euros versus 11.72 billion euros expected Net profit: 4.96 billion euros versus 4.1 billion euros expected ASML sticks to China forecast The semiconductor equipment maker said it expects China sales to account for 20% of its total business, sticking to a prior forecast. While ASML holds an effective monopoly on EUV machines, a July report from The Information suggested an unnamed Chinese company had begun manufacturing an immersion deep ultraviolet lithography (DUV) machine, citing people familiar with the matter. ASML dominates the manufacturing of DUV machines, which are less advanced than EUV. China has been ramping up its domestic semiconductor supply chain, with some investors concerned it could challenge the European and U.S. dominance. However, analysts raised questions about China's ability to ramp up its own DUV technology. ASML meanwhile has faced challenges in China over the last few years.
